issues.legal_issue: Property allotted to a Hindu female in satisfaction of her pre-existing right to maintenance is enlarged into full ownership despite restrictions imposed by the allotment instrument.
material_facts: A widow claimed maintenance from joint family property held by her deceased husband's brother, and her claim was decreed.
In execution of the decree, a court-certified compromise allotted property to her in lieu of maintenance, restricted her interest to her lifetime, and prohibited alienation.
She remained in possession of the property when the Hindu Succession Act came into force and later leased and sold portions of it.
The successor to the property sought a declaration that the alienations were not binding beyond her lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The allotment recognised and satisfied the widow's pre-existing right to maintenance, so Section 14(1), read with its Explanation, applied rather than Section 14(2). She became full owner despite the restrictions in the compromise, and the challenge to her alienations failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, read with its Explanation, broadly enlarges a Hindu female's limited interest in property possessed by her, including property acquired in lieu of maintenance. Section 14(2), as an exception to subsection (1), applies to a restricted grant creating a new title for the first time, not an instrument that merely recognises or gives effect to a pre-existing right. A widow's right to maintenance from joint family property is a pre-existing right against property. The Court relied on S.S. Munna Lal v. S.S. Raikumar and Gummalapura Taggina Matada Kotturuswami v. Setra Veeravva for the breadth of subsection (1) and the meaning of possession; Badri Pershad v. Smt. Kanso Devi and Nirmal Chand v. Vidya Wanti for the distinction between a new grant and recognition of a pre-existing right; and Rani Bai v. Shri Yadunandan Ram on the widow's maintenance right.

rule.if: appeal_against_limited_estate_ruling and property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance and maintenance_right_preexisted and female_possessed_property_when_law_changed

predicates.appeal_against_limited_estate_ruling: A party appeals a ruling that a female holds property only for a limited period or purpose.
predicates.property_given_in_lieu_of_maintenance: Property was allotted to a female to satisfy her claim for maintenance.
predicates.maintenance_right_preexisted: The female had a right to maintenance from the property before the instrument allotting it was made.
predicates.female_possessed_property_when_law_chang: The female possessed the property when the law enlarging limited interests came into force.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a limited-estate ruling and property was given to a female in satisfaction of her pre-existing maintenance right while she possessed it when the law changed, the rule treats her as its full owner.
